principles: Shared datasets live here only when at least two simulators need the same source or key vocabulary.
Large derived payloads are published as release assets, not committed to git.
Every imported dataset must keep source URL, fetch date, checksum, transform version and limitations close to the numbers.
Third-party civic-tech repositories can supply schema and importer ideas, but official or explicitly licensed exports remain the source of truth.

datasets.title: SIRUTA, UAT and CUI registry
datasets.why: This is the join key for finance, health, administrative reform, land-value and transport datasets. A wrong locality join is worse than a missing one.

upstreamSources.name: Transparenta.eu UAT CUI/natcode map
upstreamSources.license: Apache-2.0 for repository code; underlying data provenance must be checked before reuse
upstreamSources.notes: Use as a candidate crosswalk and diff against the INS registry before adoption.

provenanceRequirements: Record exact data.gov.ro resource URL and retrieval date.
Record whether CUI came from official source, Transparenta crosswalk or simulator-local resolution.
Carry one limitation for each unmatched or ambiguous UAT.
validationPlan: Diff county assignment against the official SIRUTA county field.
Report unmatched CUIs instead of silently dropping them.
datasets.storagePolicy: Small canonical JSON can be committed; larger historical snapshots should become release assets.

nextSlice.deliverable: Keep current consumers on packages/uat_registry and extend the registry only when a new dataset exposes a real simulator-local SIRUTA, CUI, county or sector-parent assumption.
nextSlice.doneWhen: New consumers either reuse the shared registry or explicitly document why a local key remains outside it.

notes: The first shared-data wave has adopted the registry as the key vocabulary for administrativ, impozit-teren, local finance, health service access, justitie and transport consumer payloads. Current shared consumers are covered by tests that reject unknown registry keys.

datasets.title: Local budget execution and fiscal stress
datasets.why: Administrative consolidation, land tax, public pay and procurement all need the same denominator: what each authority raises, receives, spends and owes.

upstreamSources.license: Public API/data license must be confirmed per imported snapshot
upstreamSources.notes: The compatibility exporter for impozit-teren now reads the shared local-finance mart rather than maintaining a separate finance import.

upstreamSources.name: Transparenta.eu server schema and analytics model
Situatia veniturilor si cheltuielilor - 2024
upstreamSources.publisher: Ministerul Dezvoltarii Regionale si Administratiei Publice

provenanceRequirements: Record GraphQL query, report type, account category, period and transformation version.
Record official comparison source and checksum for any totals used to validate Transparenta imports.
Publish classification-prefix assumptions for own revenue, transfers, personnel and capital spending.
validationPlan: Compare national and county totals against an official data.gov.ro file when available.
Quarantine outliers by per-capita spending, as the existing buget-uat importer does.
Reject rows whose SIRUTA/CUI key is absent from the shared UAT registry.
datasets.storagePolicy: Derived yearly marts should be release assets when they exceed the repository size budget; small summaries and schemas can be committed.

nextSlice.deliverable: Leave arrears, capital/development mix and funding-source dependence out of active work until a consuming simulator needs one of those extra fiscal dimensions.
nextSlice.doneWhen: The next consuming UI computes any added fiscal indicator from shared mart bases without reintroducing simulator-local finance artifacts for fields the shared mart already supplies.

notes: Transparenta data is useful, but the catalog must not imply that the repository license covers the underlying official budget data.
The official data.gov.ro Arierate package currently indexes UAT XLS resources only through 2018-06-30, so it cannot populate the 2025 mart.
The full 2023-2025 national mart is published as a `data-v1` release asset because the generated JSON is about 9.7 MB.

administrativ consumes the shared mart through a compact web payload for 2024 own revenue, spending, personnel-spending pressure plus 2023-2025 spending and own-revenue endpoint bases; per-inhabitant values and movements are recomputed in the UI from summed bases. Its merger-savings payload remains simulator-specific because it carries administration-only spending.

impozit-teren exports its 2025 browser budget denominator from the fetched 2023-2025 shared mart at build time, so the old committed buget-uat-2025 simulator artifact and redundant one-year package mart are no longer needed.

Mark geocoded locations as derived unless coordinates are directly published.

datasets.storagePolicy: Provider summary JSON can be committed if small; geocoded/routing outputs should become release assets.

nextSlice.deliverable: Pause active health expansion after the high-signal CAPeSaRo batch; when health resumes, work from the remaining 72-row source-acquisition queue.
nextSlice.doneWhen: The remaining 72 rows stay named exclusions until explicit source evidence is added; no medium/low candidate is promoted automatically.

notes: The committed national mart covers 592 ANMCS providers and all 42 Ministry county bed totals. Clinical bed counts are attached only on confident ANMCS matches; county bed totals are kept separately.
The UAT-level service-access view covers 3,181 municipality/town/commune rows, counts only the 324 serviceAccessEligible providers, and keeps the 268 county-only providers as named exclusions.
justitie consumes the shared UAT-level service-access view for its court/police/health comparison and no longer bases that comparison on the simulator-local plotted hospital map.

administrativ consumes the shared UAT-level service-access view as an aligned web payload for merged-unit local health-provider counts; Bucharest sectors stay unassigned because the shared source only places Bucharest providers at municipality level.

transport consumes the shared UAT-level service-access view in data/access.json and the map hover payload. The committed access run has 3,136 routed UAT rows with health data, 178 have at least one local eligible provider, and 235 eligible local providers are counted on those routed rows; the browser payload aligns the same shared view to all polygons and leaves Bucharest sectors unassigned.

The current ANMCS accreditation workbook, CNAS 31.03.2025 hospital contracts package and INSP UNITATI CU PATURI package do not expose national provider street-address or coordinate fields through data.gov.ro; the committed point layer therefore combines the Ministry unitati sanitare map extract, curated Ministry reviews and audited CAPeSaRo supplemental evidence.

The health-provider-points-2024-2026 contract covers all 592 mart providers. The Ministry of Health unitati sanitare map extract contributes 174 exact name/county street-address and marker-coordinate matches, 40 curated same-county source-record aliases and 4 reviewed coordinate-only exact source-row acceptances. The audited CAPeSaRo supplemental source contributes 46 provider/sourceCode pairs with street-address and coordinate evidence. 252 serviceAccessEligible, non-county-only providers now have accepted official-coordinate point evidence; the other 340 provider rows remain blocked from point routing, including all 268 county-only rows and 72 remaining no-point-evidence rows. UAT polygon containment is not applied yet because the available committed UAT geometry is not SIRUTA-keyed for this package.

The health-point-access-2024-2026 view publishes only the 252 accepted provider coordinates and names all 340 blocked providers as exclusions. It is a point layer, not a distance model; consumers must explicitly declare straight-line or routed distance before deriving access metrics.

transport now consumes health-point-access-2024-2026 directly. It reports nearest accepted provider distance in straight-line metres from each routed UAT centroid, names the method in provenance and limitations, and publishes 3,136 distances with 15.9 km unweighted median and 9.9 km population-weighted median.

justitie now consumes health-point-access-2024-2026 directly. It keeps the UAT-level local-provider and routed upper-bound hospital metrics separate, and adds nearest accepted provider point distances from consolidated UAT centroids with an explicit straight-line method.

health-point-road-access-uat-2024-2026 snaps the 252 accepted provider coordinates to administrativ UAT road-graph nodes and publishes 3,186 compact UAT road-proxy rows. The distance is road graph metres to the provider snap node plus a straight-line destination offset, not exact door-to-door routing.

justitie now consumes health-point-road-access-uat-2024-2026 as the first road-proxy consumer. It reports the shared routed provider-point proxy beside the straight-line point distance and the older UAT-level routed hospital upper bound.

transport now consumes health-point-road-access-uat-2024-2026 directly. It reports 3,136 nearest accepted provider-point road-proxy distances with the shared snap/routing methods, 23.9 km unweighted median and 13.8 km population-weighted median, while keeping the straight-line point metric as an explicitly labelled comparison.

health-provider-point-evidence-review-2024-2026 is a manual-review queue for the 72 service-eligible providers still blocked by no-point-evidence after the CAPeSaRo high-signal review pass. The remaining rows have no Ministry candidate; candidate rows are not accepted point evidence.

The high-signal street-backed review candidates promoted in the latest alias pass are anmcs-2025-230 to ms-unitati-sanitare-121, anmcs-2025-261 to ms-unitati-sanitare-274 and anmcs-2025-279 to ms-unitati-sanitare-043. The reviewed coordinate-only pass then promoted anmcs-2025-001 to ms-unitati-sanitare-159, anmcs-2025-236 to ms-unitati-sanitare-065, anmcs-2025-256 to ms-unitati-sanitare-069 and anmcs-2025-362 to ms-unitati-sanitare-066 without creating address evidence. The remaining locality-only overlaps stay out of the alias source.

ANMCS CAPeSaRo proved useful as a public dashboard source: the first audited subset promoted the 4 remaining locality-only Ministry overlaps plus 13 public-bed/no-Ministry-candidate providers, and the final high-signal batch promoted 29 public exact-name candidates. The committed supplemental evidence source keeps only audited provider/sourceCode pairs and records the dashboard URL, retrieval date and missing explicit reuse-license limitation.

health-provider-point-source-acquisition-2024-2026 is a non-evidence work queue for the remaining 72 no-point providers. It now prioritizes 16 public no-candidate providers and 56 private or unknown no-candidate providers. Its source search order covers provider websites, DSP/local-authority pages, official contracting/register sources and OSM named-feature manual review.

anmcs-capesaro-public-hospitals-2026 is a release asset with a compact extract of 731 CAPeSaRo dashboard rows, including 680 active rows and 687 rows with street-address evidence. The raw dashboard response remains out of git.

health-provider-point-capesaro-candidates-2024-2026 is a release asset with a non-evidence candidate report over the 72 remaining acquisition rows. It finds 24 providers with active same-county street-address CAPeSaRo candidates and 28 candidate rows overall. Among the 16 remaining public providers, 6 have only medium/low CAPeSaRo candidates and 10 have no CAPeSaRo candidate, so the high-signal public CAPeSaRo pass is complete.

provenanceRequirements: Record exact AMEPIP page, report or export URL and retrieval date.
Record dashboard/report vintage and exported-file checksum before importing any row-level data.
Carry an explicit limitation when reuse terms, row-level export method or enterprise identifier coverage are missing.
validationPlan: Require CUI or another stable enterprise key before joining to finance, pay or procurement views.
Compare AMEPIP financial indicators against Ministry of Finance/company finance totals where a CUI/year overlap exists.
Reject dashboard aggregate-only snapshots as simulator inputs unless row-level export and provenance are available.
datasets.storagePolicy: Commit only small source notes, schemas and sample metadata; raw dashboard exports, workbooks and derived row-level marts should be release assets.

nextSlice.deliverable: Publish the full August 2025 compensation mart as a checksum-pinned release asset, then build a compact salarizare comparison payload from that asset.
nextSlice.doneWhen: The mart release is pinned in data-assets.json and salarizare consumes only an aggregate/comparison payload with the AMEPIP reuse and PDF-parsing limitations visible to readers.

notes: AMEPIP pages describe the dashboard as covering financial, non-financial and corporate-governance indicators for public enterprises. Public notes say financial indicators are extracted from Ministry of Finance data, non-financial indicators include ESG, and governance indicators relate to listed companies.

amepip-source-inventory-2025-2026 inspected 10 AMEPIP PDFs from the KPI/report and CA/CS compensation pages: 8 KPI documents and 2 compensation documents. Six expose CUI-level rows; Annexes 1, 2 and 3 expose 170, 170 and 1212 company indicator blocks respectively.

amepip-compensation-sample-august-2025 parses the August 2025 nominal compensation PDF into 833 CUI rows and commits a 50-row sample with CUI, APT, enterprise, person, role and fixed/variable compensation fields.

amepip-compensation-mart.schema.json now defines the full row-level mart, release-asset policy and salarizare consumer contract; the generated full mart remains out of git until it is uploaded and checksum-pinned.

companiidestat.ro publishes a documented read-only API over public-company data under CC BY 4.0. It is useful for cross-checks and discovery, but this package still imports official AMEPIP PDFs directly for first-party provenance.
Do not scrape opaque Power BI internals as a source of truth. Use official PDF/report attachments or a documented export/API path before importing dashboard-derived data.
